summary: Re-tested the four Entry Certificate fixes against the public API and local rendering/email method. PDF literal escaping and email HTML escaping passed, including one-page branding regression. Two fixes are not present/effective: parallel first sends returned different certificate tokens, and upcoming_alerts remains reverse chronological. Both parallel real email sends themselves succeeded.

critical.issue: Atomic token creation still fails. Two simultaneous first sends both returned 200 but produced different certificate_token values ('HpchMj1DaJNZa05GOvN3hdYUFyg' and 'UI_kbywY194TKHAuSeQj29C_iic'). Because only one token can remain persisted, one delivered certificate URL becomes invalid.

minor.issue: For a commission 45 days out, upcoming_alerts is still [0, 1, 7, 14, 30] instead of chronological [30, 14, 7, 1, 0]. ALERT_BUCKETS itself correctly remains ascending.

action_items: Replace _get_entry_certificate_token's read-then-unconditional-update with a conditional find_one_and_update; if a concurrent caller loses the update, refetch and return the winner's persisted token.
Sort the alerts_status response's upcoming_alerts by days_out descending without changing ascending ALERT_BUCKETS.
Re-run the two failing focused tests after applying the missing changes.
critical_code_review_comments: The checked-in _get_entry_certificate_token implementation at server.py:847-858 still calls find_one followed by unconditional update_one; it does not contain the conditional find_one_and_update described in the review request.
alerts_status at server.py:527-540 appends in ascending ALERT_BUCKETS order and returns the list without sorting; the claimed reverse days_out sort is absent.

PDF escaping is effective for the requested signer name, ID number and document description. The generated PDF preserved all values verbatim, stayed one-page Letter portrait, was 38-42 KB, contained the shield image, red rule, navy attestation block and required footer.

Captured certificate email HTML encoded signer, document type/description, personal note, notary name, commission number and state; no raw script tags were emitted. Certificate ID is server-generated hex and is also passed through html.escape.

success_rate.backend: 50% of four scoped fixes passed (2/4); PDF/email escaping regressions passed, race/order fixes failed

seed_data_creation: Created temporary TEST certificate entries and auto-client records, then deleted them. Sent exactly two real certificate emails to matthew.yurksaitis@dominibusservices.com for the required concurrency test; both provider calls returned success. Email-injection inspection used a patched sender and did not send a real email.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Do not spend more email volume until fixes land. Re-run only TestEntryCertificateFixesIteration7::test_parallel_first_email_calls_share_one_persisted_token (two real sends) and ::test_alert_status_is_chronological_without_changing_bucket_order. PDF exact literals and branded rendering passed; email HTML capture passed after final test correction.
rca_of_the_issue: The race is reproduced because both callers can read a missing token, independently generate tokens, then unconditionally overwrite the same entry before sending; each response/email keeps its local token while MongoDB retains only the last write. Alert ordering remains wrong because the response directly iterates ascending ALERT_BUCKETS and never applies the requested descending days_out sort. These are source-level omissions, not flaky test behavior.
